signals.name: Logistic Regression (walk-forward)
signals.origin: L2-regularised logistic regression on standardised features; purged walk-forward CV (Lopez de Prado 2018)
signals.reason: P(up) 31%; walk-forward accuracy 62% on 494 bars (5 folds, base rate 69%)
signals.rules: Linear model of P(up in `horizon` bars) from ~70 technical, market-factor, time and strategy-vote features. Validated out-of-sample on the most recent 60% of history in 5 expanding folds.

signals.name: Random Forest (walk-forward)
signals.reason: P(up) 38%; walk-forward accuracy 61% on 494 bars (5 folds, base rate 69%)
signals.rules: Bagged decision trees on the same feature set. Reports the walk-forward accuracy so you can see whether it has any edge on this chart.

signals.name: Gradient Boosting (walk-forward)
signals.origin: Friedman (2001); histogram-based implementation (Ke et al. 2017), purged walk-forward CV
signals.reason: P(up) 33%; walk-forward accuracy 48% on 494 bars (5 folds, base rate 69%)
signals.rules: Boosted shallow trees on the same feature set; captures non-linear interactions between indicators and market context.

signals.name: Stacked Strategy Votes (Wolpert)
signals.origin: Stacked generalisation (Wolpert 1992): level-1 logistic regression over every strategy's vote
signals.reason: P(up) 31%; walk-forward accuracy 55% on 494 bars (5 folds, base rate 69%)
signals.rules: Learns a weight for every strategy from its historical votes on this instrument and timeframe - a negative weight means the strategy has been contrarian here.

signals.name: Calibrated Ensemble
signals.origin: Average of the four walk-forward learners, Platt-scaled (Platt 1999) on out-of-fold predictions
signals.reason: Calibrated P(up) 29%. Out-of-sample, calls at least this strong were right 76% of the time (115 bars, 39% of history); evidence: drift
signals.rules: The final probability. A direction is called only where out-of-sample calls of the same strength were right at least 55% of the time; otherwise the system stands aside (no call).
